subChunks.title: Hover, Focus, and Interactive States
subChunks.hookHtml: Interactive states transform static HTML into a responsive, communicative interface. Tailwind's variant prefixes (hover:, focus:, active:, disabled:) apply any utility conditionally — no custom CSS required. Once you understand the variant syntax, you can express complex interactive behaviour in a single class string.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Variant syntax

Any utility can be applied conditionally using a variant prefix and a colon:

hover:bg-blue-700       /* on mouse hover    */
focus:ring-2            /* when focused      */
active:scale-95         /* while being clicked */
disabled:opacity-50     /* when disabled     */
visited:text-purple-600 /* visited links     */
placeholder:text-gray-400 /* input placeholder */

Button states

<button class="
  bg-blue-600 text-white px-4 py-2 rounded-md font-medium
  hover:bg-blue-700
  active:scale-95
  focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:ring-offset-2
  disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed
  transition-colors duration-150
">
  Accept Quest
</button>

Link states

<a class="
  text-blue-600
  hover:text-blue-800 hover:underline
  visited:text-purple-600
  focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:rounded
">
  View quest details
</a>

Card hover effects

<div class="
  bg-white rounded-xl p-6 shadow-sm
  hover:shadow-md hover:-translate-y-0.5
  transition duration-200
  cursor-pointer
">
  <!-- card content -->
</div>

Group hover (child reacts to parent hover)

<div class="group flex items-center gap-3 p-4 hover:bg-gray-50 rounded-lg cursor-pointer">
  <div class="w-10 h-10 bg-blue-100 rounded-full flex items-center justify-center">
    <!-- icon -->
  </div>
  <div class="flex-1">
    <p class="font-medium text-gray-900">Quest Name</p>
  </div>
  <!-- Arrow appears only when parent is hovered: -->
  <svg class="w-4 h-4 text-gray-400 opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity">...</svg>
</div>

Peer (sibling state)

<!-- Label changes when checkbox is checked: -->
<input type="checkbox" id="accept" class="peer sr-only" />
<label for="accept" class="
  border-2 border-gray-200 rounded-lg p-3 cursor-pointer
  peer-checked:border-blue-500 peer-checked:bg-blue-50
  peer-checked:text-blue-700
">
  Accept Terms
</label>

Lyra: "group-hover is one of the most powerful patterns in Tailwind. Without it, you would need JavaScript or custom CSS to show an arrow when a row is hovered. With group on the parent and group-hover: on the child, the whole row lights up with one class each. No JavaScript. No @apply. Just utilities."

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: Every button needs four states: resting, hovered, focused, and disabled. Without states, a button feels dead. With them, it communicates. hover:bg-blue-700, active:scale-95, focus:ring-2, disabled:opacity-50 — those four modifiers cover the entire interactive vocabulary of a production button.

storyBeats.speaker: A complete interactive button
storyBeats.text:
<button class="
  bg-blue-600 text-white px-4 py-2 rounded-md font-medium
  hover:bg-blue-700
  active:scale-95
  focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:ring-offset-2
  disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed
  transition-colors duration-150
">
  Accept Quest
</button>

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a fully interactive button and list row:

  • .btn-primary: blue background, white text, padding, rounded — plus hover:bg-blue-700, active:scale-95, focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:ring-offset-2, disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed, transition-colors duration-150
  • .list-row: group, flex, items-center, gap-3, p-4, hover:bg-gray-50, rounded-lg, cursor-pointer
  • .row-arrow: ml-auto, opacity-0, group-hover:opacity-100, transition-opacity

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a settings card with: a toggle switch using peer (checkbox peer, label uses peer-checked: to change background and border colour), a hover-lift card (shadow increases and card moves up slightly on hover), and a link with hover underline and visited purple colour.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the group-hover pattern — what does adding group to a parent enable for its children, and why is this powerful? Walk through the peer pattern for a custom checkbox — what does peer do, and why is the order of peer and the peer-checked: element important in the HTML?

questions.prompt: How do you apply a utility only when an element is hovered in Tailwind?
options: Prefix the utility with hover: — e.g. hover:bg-blue-700
Add :hover to the class name — e.g. bg-blue-700:hover
Use @hover in your CSS and reference the class
Add a data-hover attribute to the element
questions.answer: Prefix the utility with hover: — e.g. hover:bg-blue-700
questions.explanation: Tailwind uses variant prefixes before the utility class name. hover:bg-blue-700 generates the CSS .hover\:bg-blue-700:hover { background-color: ... }. The same pattern applies to focus:, active:, disabled:, and all other variants.

questions.prompt: You want a list row where hovering anywhere on the row shows a hidden arrow icon at the right. The parent has group. Which class on the arrow achieves this?
questions.explanation: group on the parent and group-hover: on children is the Tailwind pattern for parent-triggered child states. opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 makes the arrow invisible by default and visible when the parent is hovered, with a smooth transition. Using hidden/group-hover:block works too but skips the smooth transition.

questions.prompt: A button has transition-colors duration-150. It also has hover:bg-blue-700 and active:scale-95. The colour transition works but the scale doesn't animate. Why?
options: transition-colors only transitions colour properties — scale requires transition-transform or the all-encompassing transition class
active: variants don't support transitions in Tailwind
scale-95 requires duration-150 applied separately with scale-duration-150
questions.answer: transition-colors only transitions colour properties — scale requires transition-transform or the all-encompassing transition class
questions.explanation: transition-colors only watches color, background-color, border-color, and related colour properties. For scale transforms, add transition-transform (or replace both with transition which transitions all transitionable properties). The transition class in Tailwind is a convenient shorthand: it covers color, background-color, border-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke, opacity, box-shadow, transform, filter, backdrop-filter.
